newsitem.title: USA: Republican says futile to limit campaign funding.
newsitem.headline: Republican says futile to limit campaign funding.

text.p: Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell said Thursday that limiting campaign fundraising would be futile and said Congress should focus on keeping foreign money out of U.S. election campaigns.
"If we need to strengthen the law to further ensure that foreigners can't undermine domestic elections, then we need to do that," McConnell, of Kentucky, said.
Controversy over foreign contributions to the Democratic Party and skyrocketing spending on campaigns in the last election has spurred widespread calls for reform of campaign funding laws.
But McConnell repeated his opposition to limiting contributions from Americans while calling for curbs on how unions spend their members' dues.
"The public is not clamouring for any bill which keeps them from participating in the political process," he said on CNN television's "Early Edition."

"And so any effort to try to do it, particularly along the lines that the Democratic leader is suggesting, is trying to wall up water rolling down a hill. It's always going to find another way to find its way to the bottom," he said.

Senate Democratic leader Tom Daschle has proposed banning so-called "soft money" contributions that provide a channel for businesses, unions and wealthy people to pour money into political parties without any federal limits.
